 Judgment
Aggrieved by the judgment an award passed in MVC No.80/2011 dated 25.01.2012 by the II Additional MACT, Karwar, the claimants have approached this Court in appeal.
2. The petitioners before the Tribunal are the wife, children and mother of deceased Vasant.
The petitioners contended that the deceased was a fisherman aged about 32 years at the time of accident and was earning Rs.6,000/- p.m.

It is stated that on 17.02.2011 at about 11.30 a.m. while he was walking on Mudaga-Bandar road, he was collided with a lorry bearing its Reg.No.KA- 30/7108 from behind and succumbed to injuries on the same day.

It was alleged that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the lorry driver and due to the untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to untold mental and economical hardship.
Thus, they claimed a compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the owner and insurer of the said lorry.
3. The owner and insurer of the lorry appeared before the Tribunal and resisted the claim.

Respondent No.2 filed the objection statement contending that the said lorry was falsely implicated in the matter and there was no nexus between the accident and the said lorry and that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the deceased himself.

Inter alia it was also contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, imaginary and unsustainable under law and the age,
income and occupation of the deceased are to be proved by the petitioners.

They also contended that Veena W/O Late Vasant Harikantra vs Hammanna H Nayak on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100771258/
2 the terms and conditions of the policy were violated and therefore, the claim petition be dismissed as against them.
4. Pursuant to the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues and the petitioners examined three witnesses in support of their case as PW.1 to PW.3 and Exs.P.1 to P.7 were marked in evidence.

sentences.text:
No evidence was led on behalf of respondent No.2 but, the copy of the policy was marked by consent as Ex.R.1.
5.
On hearing arguments by both sides, the Tribunal proceeded to award a sum of Rs.6,73,000/- as compensation along with interest at 6% p.a.
It is the said judgment and award which has been questioned before this Court.
6. On issuance of notice, respondent No.2 appeared before this Court through its counsel and respondent No.1 did not appear despite service of notice.
7. The appeal being admitted, I have heard the arguments by the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Learned counsel for the appellant did not appear in the matter.
The matter being slated for final hearing, the appeal is taken up for final disposal.

8. The fact that there was an accident on 17.02.2011 at about 11.30 a.m. and the lorry bearing its Reg.No.KA-30/7108 which was driven in a rash and negligent manner and it dashed upon the deceased Vasant is not in dispute.

The fact that the said lorry was insured with respondent No.2 as on the date of the accident and the driver of the lorry was possessing valid driving licence as on the date of the accident is also not in dispute.
Therefore, the only question that remains to be adjudicated is about the quantum of compensation.

9. The Tribunal noticed that the deceased was a fisherman and he was working for a boat permanently and that he was drawing a monthly salary of Rs.6,000/- as contended by the petitioners, but there is no documentary evidence to show the permanent monthly income of the deceased.

Therefore, by appreciating the evidence of PW.3 and the certificate issued by him that he was owning a boat and the deceased was working on the said boat, held that the income of the deceased could not have been Rs.6,000/- p.m. for the entire year.
Though it was urged on behalf of respondent No.2 that Minimum Wages Act have to be considered and the income has to be considered only for six months, the same has been rejected.
However, it held that the income of Rs.6,000/- has to be considered only for six months and therefore, for the remaining six months the notional income of Rs.3,000/- was adopted by the Tribunal.

Thus, it held Rs.54,000/- (Rs.36,000/-
+ Rs.18,000/-) as the income of the deceased.

Deducting 1/4th towards personal expenses, the annual income was considered at Rs.40,500/- and adopting the multiplier of 16, a sum of Rs.6,48,000/- was awarded to the petitioners under the head of loss of dependency.
10. It is pertinent to note that the Tribunal failed to consider the future prospects of the deceased.

Therefore, by taking the income of the deceased at Rs.54,000/- p.m. and adding the same by 40%
towards future prospects, the multiplicand works out to Rs.75,600/-.
Hence, by deducting 1/4th of the same towards personal expenses, the effective multiplicand comes to Rs.56,700/-.

Therefore, the Veena W/O Late Vasant Harikantra vs Hammanna H Nayak on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100771258/
3 compensation to be awarded under the head of loss of dependency is Rs.56,700/- x 16 =
Rs.9,07,200/-.
11.

 Loss of consortium and 2,20,000/-
 loss of love and affection  (Rs.44,000/- x 5)
 Loss of estate and funeral 33,000/-
 expenses (Rs.16,500/-

12 . Thus, the petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.4,87,200/- (Rs.11,60,200 - Rs.6,73,000) with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization, in addition to the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, we pass the following:
(2022) 2 SCC 767 ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed in MVC No.80/2011 dated 25.01.2012 by the II Additional MACT, Karwar is modified awarding a sum of Rs.4,87,200/- in addition to the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

The compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization (iii) The other terms of the Tribunal regarding payment of interest, cost,
apportionment and deposit remain unaltered.
(iv) The compensation amount including the enhanced compensation amount with interest shall be deposited within four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
